key_insight: SOLE-R1 turns a video-language reasoning model into the sole reward function for on-robot reinforcement learning, letting robots learn from self-observed video and language task specs rather than hand-crafted rewards; this reduces exploitation of static VLM evaluators under partial observability and distribution shift.
problem_solved: Current vision-language evaluators used as rewards for RL are brittle under partial observability and distribution shift, enabling policies to game perceptual errors instead of solving tasks; SOLE-R1 provides a robust, temporal video-language supervision signal that closes the loop on real robot learning without engineered rewards.
method: Train a video-language reasoning model to score entire robot video trajectories against natural-language task descriptions, emphasizing temporal grounding and cross-frame consistency.

Use the model’s trajectory-level scores as the sole reward signal in an on-robot RL loop: collect video, score with SOLE-R1, and update policy—no external reward engineering or instrumented lab setup.
Improve evaluator robustness via robot-domain finetuning, calibration/uncertainty-aware scoring, and design choices that prevent policies from exploiting perceptual shortcuts.
impact: Provides a scalable, general-purpose reward mechanism for real-world robot learning, reducing manual reward design and labels while improving robustness to observation gaps and distribution shifts—making on-robot RL more practical for diverse tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: robot executes policy → captures video → SOLE-R1 scores trajectory vs. language goal → RL update loop (closed-loop).
Architecture schematic: temporal video encoder + language encoder → cross-modal reasoning head → trajectory-level reward output.
Comparison chart: policy performance and failure modes under partial observability for (a) static image VLM rewards vs (b) SOLE-R1 video-language rewards.
Example task sequence panels: before/after learning with scored video frames showing correct vs exploited failure cases annotated.
paper_title: SOLE-R1: Video-Language Reasoning as the Sole Reward for On-Robot Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Philip Schroeder, Thomas Weng, Karl Schmeckpeper, Eric Rosen, Stephen Hart
